mood.value: playful mock-seriousness that melts into relief: a fake courtroom with real friends laughing underneath
mood.reason: The concept runs on a straight-faced joke. The awkwardness of asking for money has to turn into a light release when the app settles it.

tone.value: flatmates teasing each other in Hinglish, a mock-solemn judge against a cheeky accused. It never sounds like a bank or a lecture.
tone.reason: The audience trusts friends, not fintech. The teasing lets the ad name an awkward problem without shaming anyone.

setting.value: a lived-in Indian flat living room with a sagging sofa, a plastic-covered side table, a drying rack in the corner, and a steel tumbler and a half-eaten snack plate on the table
setting.reason: It looks like the places where rent and food get split. The steel tumbler gavel is a familiar household prop and the scene needs no extra set.

camera.value: handheld smartphone front camera look, shot and reverse shot between judge and accused, with one short over-the-shoulder shot on the phone screen
camera.reason: It feels like a Reel a friend filmed. Reverse shots keep the back-and-forth quick and make the app screen readable once.

lens.value: smartphone front camera, 24 mm equivalent, f/1.9, at arm's length
lens.reason: It is the lens people already use for Reels and gives a slightly wide, intimate frame. Two people in a small room fit without looking staged.

light.value: late-afternoon daylight from a window on the left, with a warm tube-light bounce from the ceiling
light.reason: One real window source keeps skin tones natural and the room looks lived-in. Warm indoor bounce adds the Indian flat feel and keeps the phone screen bright by contrast.

palette.value: muted everyday tones of faded sofa teal, wood brown, steel grey and cream walls
palette.reason: A plain room makes the app the brightest thing in frame, so the eye lands on the product at the moment of the group view and UPI settle-up.

pacing.value: cuts every 3-4 seconds: hook in the first 3s, two quick 'kal de dunga' exchanges, the phone reveal around 10s, UPI settle and 'Case dismissed' by 19s, end card for the last 3s
pacing.reason: This fits the 22s target and the Reels scroll. Each beat gets one clear shot and the payoff lands before attention drops.

cast.name: kabir
cast.look: Indian man with a lean, tall frame, light wheatish skin, a long narrow face, thick black eyebrows, a neatly trimmed short beard and short, tightly curled hair. He wears round wire glasses and has a sly, raised-eyebrow look.
cast.outfit: mustard-yellow half-sleeve cotton shirt worn open over a plain white vest, and dark grey shorts
cast.voice: clear mid-range, theatrical when playing judge, dropping to a dry flat tone when he is annoyed
cast.pace: measured and deliberate in judge mode, then quicker when he laughs
speech_habits: opens with a loud 'Order order!' and then waits a beat
says 'Arre bhai...' with a long sigh when he is let down

cast.name: rohan
cast.look: Indian man with a stocky, broad-shouldered build, deep brown skin, a round face, a shaved head with light stubble, a small gap between his front teeth, and a wide, easy grin
cast.outfit: faded maroon hoodie with the sleeves pushed up, and light blue jeans
cast.voice: warm and a little nasal, easygoing and slightly pleading
cast.pace: fast and tumbling when making excuses, slow when caught
speech_habits: says 'Kal de dunga, pakka' too fast and too often
trails off with 'bas ek hafte mein...' when he knows it is weak

brand_accent: one bright brand-green accent on the Chukta phone screen
